main_text.p: igne,quotidie molliunt, fundunt, & exte-runt.Si praeterea nofter uentriculus fua for ma duntaxat alimentū concoqueret,quor-fum temperamento & naturali calore prae-ditus effet ? At his fruftra non eft praeditus, quoniam à natura nihil fruftra fit.Quinetiā fi noftri uentriculi temperametum nullam edat actionem, profecto nulla intemperie laborabit ipfe uentriculus. Propterea parti fimilari tria morborū genera infidere, nem pe immoderationem,intemperiem,& cor-ruptelam perperā ftatuit Fernelius.Poftre-mo nifi nofter uentriculus fit fanus,beneq; affectus alimentū haud probe poterit con-ficere.At uentriculi fanitas & bona diathe-fis,eft eius temperamentum.Quod pafsim oftendit Galenus, & praefertim tertio Me-thodi medendi libro,ubi partiū fimilarium fanitatem effe quatuor qualitatum iuftam temperiem ait. Igitur uentriculus abfq; fuo temperamento alimentum cocoquere ne-quit. Nam ipfum temperamentum, uel eft naturale & integrum, uel laefum & praeter naturam:fi hoc eft,tum male agit, fin illud bene.Verum alia uentriculi fanitatem,prae-ter hanc agnofcimus, qua uidelicet inftru-mentalem edit actionem, puta chyli distri-butionem,

page.notes: The word "beneq;" is uncertain in the scan (the final sign may be a different abbreviation); read as printed. The phrase "pe immoderationem" is as printed. The final line "butionem," is the continuation of the word hyphenated at the line end, so it is part of the text and not a catchword. The paragraph boundaries are not clearly marked by indents, so the page is set as one paragraph continuing from the previous page.
